post.description: Files the patient's proposed prescriptions and intake for a clinician of the network that reviews your platform's consults in this mode. Only a platform API key files consults: another key returns 403 forbidden, and a platform with no network linked in the key's mode returns 403 network_not_linked. The prescriptions are checked as a signed order with the same lines would be now (catalog, quantities, refills, requirements, shipping and price), so the consult is refused now for what its order would be refused for. A medication that the practice's catalog does not list in the key's mode returns 422 medication_not_visible. Every other broken rule returns one 422 invalid_order with one issue for each problem: an empty answer, a repeated intake id, a schedule rule, a patient in one of the network's live-visit states (live_visit_required at patient.address.state), each missing required answer (required at intake, naming the id) and the order's own rules. A Live consult needs its payer's payment method or covering credit, or it returns 409 payment_method_required. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key and body returns the consult with its current status and 200; the same key with a different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused. A used externalConsultId returns 409 consult_already_exists with data.consultId. In Test mode, a first prescription's notes that start with test_consult_approve or test_consult_decline make a test clinician approve or decline the consult at once; Live never does this. A clinician decides a Live consult, and the consult.approved or consult.declined event tells you.
post.summary: File a consult for a network clinician

schema.description: Find medications that match every word of this text, in any order. Case and accents are ignored. The search reads the name, ingredients, strength, form, route, brands, category and pharmacy name. A word matches the start of a word in this text. A word of letters also matches a part of the name. A word of letters only that matches no word start can have typos: 1 from 4 letters, 2 from 6 letters. A word with a digit takes no typos. Thousands commas are optional: 1000 IU finds 1,000 IU/mL. A word of punctuation alone, such as %, matches only a name that contains it. A medication ID finds that medication. Results stay A to Z by name. An empty query lists every medication. Restart pagination after changing query.

get.description: Every medication you can order in the current mode, A to Z by name, then by ID. Send query to find medications by name, ingredient, strength, form or pharmacy. Then choose by name, strength, form and pharmacy. Send practiceId to list what that practice can order, at its prices; without it, the caller's organization is used. Prices are in cents. `requirements` names the optional prescription fields this pharmacy requires; `compoundingReasons` lists the accepted reasons; when it is empty, send no reason. `quantities` lists the accepted values when the pharmacy limits them, counted in `quantityUnit`. With a `fill`, `price` is per fill and each quantity counts `quantityUnit`, not fills: it is a whole number of fills in units. For a fill of 30 tablets, quantity 60 is two fills. For vials, quantity 1 is one vial and quantity 2 is two vials. A 2 mL vial lists quantities 1–10; its volume is separate from its quantity.

category.description: What the medication is prescribed for. Every strength, form and pharmacy of one medication has the same category.

coldChainRequired.description: Whether the medication requires refrigerated shipping.

compoundingReasons.description: The accepted compounding reasons. A compoundingReason must be one of them; an empty list means the medication takes no reason, so omit compoundingReason.

defaultDirections.description: The catalog's default directions, or null when none are supplied.

fill.description: What the pharmacy dispenses for one price, or null when the complete fill is unknown.

form.description: The dosage form, or null when it is unknown.

fullName.description: The name with each ingredient: its salt where the catalog records one, such as Enclomiphene Citrate, or the ingredients of a blend named for what prescribers call it, such as Myers' Cocktail. Equals name otherwise.

kit.description: The vials or bottles a kit holds, in the order they are used; null for anything that is not a kit.

pharmacyRank.description: Affinity's preference for the dispensing pharmacy, from 0 for the most preferred. When two pharmacies have the same item at the same price, choose the lower rank. Absent when Affinity has no preference for the pharmacy.

researchUseOnly.description: Whether the medication is for research use only (RUO). Only an organization with RUO access sees one.

maxRefills.description: The most refills a prescription of this medication takes, or null when any count within the request limits is accepted. 0 means the pharmacy takes no refills: send a new order for each fill.

quantities.description: The accepted quantities, counted in quantityUnit; an empty list permits any quantity within the request limits.

quantityUnit.description: The unit used to count the prescribed quantity, or null when it is unknown.

receivesAllergies.description: Whether this medication's pharmacy receives the patient's allergies. When false, the pharmacy's API has no field for them, so they never reach it; Affinity still accepts and sends the order. Tell the prescriber before they sign.

requirements.description: The optional prescription field paths that this medication requires.

restrictedStates.description: Every state where this medication cannot ship, including states the pharmacy does not cover. It can ship to every other state.

shippingOptions.description: The shipping options available for this medication.

shippingSuppliesPrice.description: Always 0. Each shipping option price is the complete shipping price.

strength.description: The pharmacy's strength text, or null when it is unknown.

directions.description: The maximum character count for directions.

notes.description: The maximum character count for notes, including allergies when notesIncludeAllergies is true.

notesIncludeAllergies.description: Whether the patient's allergies share the notes field and its character limit.

fieldLimits.description: Pharmacy-specific character limits for directions and notes. When notesIncludeAllergies is true, notes share their limit with the patient's allergies, composed as the pharmacy receives them. Absent when the ordinary prescription limits apply.

additionalProperties.description: A field that this API version can add. Ignore fields that you do not know.

unsupportedFields.description: The prescription fields this medication's pharmacy cannot receive: notes (send none) and substitutionPermitted (send true). An order that sets one is still accepted; in Live mode Affinity staff handle it, and in Test mode it fails when sent. Absent when the pharmacy receives them all.

variants.description: With expand=variants: every other available strength, form and pharmacy of the same medication, for the current organization and mode.

additionalProperties.description: A field that this API version can add. Ignore fields that you do not know.

get.description: Read one available medication, its pricing, and pharmacy details for the current organization and mode. Pass expand=variants to include its other strengths, forms and pharmacies.

post.description: One request creates the order, signs it and sends it to the pharmacy. Platforms must send practiceId; practice callers can omit it to use their own practice. With an API key, name the prescriber and send signatureAttestation. Optional prescriber phone and address each default to the practice; no account is looked up by NPI. In the app, the signed-in member signs with the NPI in their settings, or names the prescriber with the same attestation. With patient.id (a pat_ ID) or patient.externalId, the order reuses that patient of the practice and mode and updates the saved record; without them, each order creates a new patient. If id and externalId identify different patients, the request returns 422 invalid_order. A medication that the practice's catalog does not list in the caller's mode returns 422 medication_not_visible, with an issue at prescriptions[n].medicationId; read GET /v1/medications with the same key and practiceId. Other broken order rules return 422 invalid_order, with one issue for each problem. When PerfectRx already holds a different firstName or lastName for the patient, the order is still accepted: a Live order stays submitted until staff correct the name with PerfectRx, and a Test order fails with a failureReason. Live orders require Live access on the practice and its platform. A Live order needs its payer's default payment method (a card or a US bank account) or account credit that covers the order, or it returns 409 payment_method_required; the platform pays for its practices. A payer that Affinity bills on one invoice for its shipped Live orders needs neither.
post.summary: Create, sign and submit an order

Separate strength fields, practice names, prac_ IDs and rx_ IDs are not searched. Restart pagination when filters change.

post.description: 200 with status cancelled when the cancel is confirmed. 202 with cancelRequestedAt when the pharmacy has not confirmed yet: you get order.cancelled when it confirms, or, when it refuses, cancelRequestedAt becomes null and you get order.updated. If an earlier ask may have reached the pharmacy, a refusal keeps cancelRequestedAt and sends no event until the pharmacy ends the order (order.cancelled or order.shipped). 409 cannot_cancel when the order is shipped, delivered or failed. 409 cancel_refused when the pharmacy refused the cancel, or when Affinity could not reach the pharmacy; only the second says to retry with a new Idempotency-Key.

post.description: Platforms and independent practices can register up to 16 public HTTPS endpoints per mode. An API key acts only for its own organization and mode. Every event goes to every endpoint. The signing secret is returned by creation and its idempotent replay for 24 hours.

Affinity POSTs each event as JSON to your registered endpoint URL, with an `Affinity-Signature: t=<Unix time in seconds>,v1=<signature>` header and an `Affinity-Event-Id` header that holds the event `id`. The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `t`, a period (`.`) and the raw request body bytes, keyed with the endpoint's whole signing secret (`whsec_…`). Verify each request before you use it: calculate the signature from the raw body, compare it with `v1` in constant time, and reject the request if they differ or if `t` is more than 300 seconds from your current time. Any 2xx response within 10 seconds acknowledges the delivery. Affinity does not follow redirects. After any other status, a redirect or no response, Affinity retries an order, prescription or consult event, up to 12 tries in all, waiting 2, 4, 8 minutes and so on, at most 24 hours, between tries. A `webhook_endpoint.test` event is sent once and not retried.

compoundingReasons.description: The accepted compounding reasons. A compoundingReason must be one of them; an empty list means the medication takes no reason, so omit compoundingReason.

defaultDirections.description: The catalog's default directions, or null when none are supplied.

fill.description: What the pharmacy dispenses for one price, or null when the complete fill is unknown.

form.description: The dosage form, or null when it is unknown.

fullName.description: The name with each ingredient: its salt where the catalog records one, such as Enclomiphene Citrate, or the ingredients of a blend named for what prescribers call it, such as Myers' Cocktail. Equals name otherwise.

kit.description: The vials or bottles a kit holds, in the order they are used; null for anything that is not a kit.

pharmacyRank.description: Affinity's preference for the dispensing pharmacy, from 0 for the most preferred. When two pharmacies have the same item at the same price, choose the lower rank. Absent when Affinity has no preference for the pharmacy.

researchUseOnly.description: Whether the medication is for research use only (RUO). Only an organization with RUO access sees one.

maxRefills.description: The most refills a prescription of this medication takes, or null when any count within the request limits is accepted. 0 means the pharmacy takes no refills: send a new order for each fill.

quantities.description: The accepted quantities, counted in quantityUnit; an empty list permits any quantity within the request limits.

quantityUnit.description: The unit used to count the prescribed quantity, or null when it is unknown.

receivesAllergies.description: Whether this medication's pharmacy receives the patient's allergies. When false, the pharmacy's API has no field for them, so they never reach it; Affinity still accepts and sends the order. Tell the prescriber before they sign.

requirements.description: The optional prescription field paths that this medication requires.

restrictedStates.description: Every state where this medication cannot ship, including states the pharmacy does not cover. It can ship to every other state.

shippingOptions.description: The shipping options available for this medication.

shippingSuppliesPrice.description: Always 0. Each shipping option price is the complete shipping price.

strength.description: The pharmacy's strength text, or null when it is unknown.

directions.description: The maximum character count for directions.

notes.description: The maximum character count for notes, including allergies when notesIncludeAllergies is true.

notesIncludeAllergies.description: Whether the patient's allergies share the notes field and its character limit.

fieldLimits.description: Pharmacy-specific character limits for directions and notes. When notesIncludeAllergies is true, notes share their limit with the patient's allergies, composed as the pharmacy receives them. Absent when the ordinary prescription limits apply.

additionalProperties.description: A field that this API version can add. Ignore fields that you do not know.

unsupportedFields.description: The prescription fields this medication's pharmacy cannot receive: notes (send none) and substitutionPermitted (send true). An order that sets one is still accepted; in Live mode Affinity staff handle it, and in Test mode it fails when sent. Absent when the pharmacy receives them all.

amount.description: The amount in the specified unit.

unit.description: The unit used to measure the amount.

failureReason.description: Why this prescription failed, for a person to read: the order's failureReason when it has the order's status, Affinity's generic rejection text when it alone failed, and null otherwise. A refused cancel leaves it null.

quantity.description: The prescribed quantity in quantityUnit, not a count of fills. With a fill, it is a whole number of fills in units: two fills of 30 tablets is 60. A vial's unit is vial, so 2 is two vials.
